newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields creep up a tad awaiting jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields creep up a tad awaiting jobs.

text.p: *Australian bond yields crept up slightly in early trading as the market lacked immediate incentives to plough on with last week's hefty rally in front of Thursday's key labour force data. *ANZ job ads data due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields crept up slightly in early trading as the market lacked immediate incentives to plough on with last week's hefty rally in front of Thursday's key labour force data.
"The market has had an extremely good run, but it hasn't really got too much to go on before the jobs data. So for now technicals are going to rule the roost," said one trader.
September 10-year bond futures struck a fresh contract high of 93.210 high in after hours trading, taking the equivalent yield well below 6.80 percent and it lowest level since mid-February 1994.

However, technical analysts feel that the short-end of the futures curve needs to catch up on the long end's advance before the 10-year contract can realistically progress further to the next resistance level of 93.250.

The 10-year contract put on over 30 basis points last week, while the three-year added under 20 basis points, with the long end benefitting from a firm U.S. treasury market and offshore demand which was seen triggered by Moody's decision to Australia's credit ratings on a positive outlook.
The short end, meanwhile, continues to mull over the possibility of an easing in monetary policy.
However, such thoughts are likely to hinge on the outcome of Thursday's June labour force data.

Median forecasts centre on a 40,250 rebound in employment, which would practically wipe out the 40,300 fall in May, although a much stronger figure would be need to cancel calls for a cut in current 5.5 percent official interest rates.
Economists expect unemployment to remain high at a median 8.7 percent, and only just below May's 8.8 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
Meanwhile, local interest is likely to be thin at the start of the week in the aftermath of Friday's U.S. holiday.
The local market's minor retracement in thin trading conditions saw it showing a mild underperforming bias against the U.S. and Canada, giving up some of last week's strong spread tightening.
